newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-PM CANDIDATE SEES 12MLN '97 BUDGET DEFICIT-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-PM CANDIDATE SEES 12MLN '97 BUDGET DEFICIT-REPORT.

text.p: Latvia's plan for a balanced budget in 1997 is out of reach and the deficit could amount to as much as 12 million lats, prime minister designate Guntars Krasts was reported as saying by the daily Diena on Thursday.
"Finance ministry calculations show that a balanced budget this year is impossible," Krasts was quoted as saying in an interview with the paper. "The deficit could be around 12 milloion lats."
Former Prime Minister Andris Shkele, who quit on Monday, said that the budget situation has improved since his government came to power in late 1995.
Shkele said that state budget currently runs a 30 million lat (around $60 mln) surplus.
Bringing order to public finances is seen as Shkele's main achievement. He started office with a budget deficit of 90 million lats ($180 mln).
